free_tier.stated: Free plan, quoted from the plans page: '1 app', 'CPU per app: 0.25 CPU', 'RAM per app: 128 MB RAM', table rows 'DiskPer app | 250 MB disk', 'Network speedPer app | 10 Mbit/s', and 'Monthly transferShared across your account | 100 GB/mo'. The page states '100 GB monthly transfer across your account.' Paid: 'Starter' '$5/ 30 days' for '3 apps' at '0.5 CPU', '512 MB RAM', '2 GB disk', '500 GB monthly transfer'; 'Pro' '$10/ 30 days' for '6 apps' at '1 CPU', '1 GB RAM', '10 GB disk', '1 TB monthly transfer'. Prices in USD. 'No. You can create an account and run one app on the Free plan without adding payment details.' Billing: '30 days, paid in advance: Pay through PayPal. Renewing the same active plan adds 30 days to its expiry date. We don’t renew it automatically.'

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed

chaining: a 128 MB container is enough for a scraper, a webhook receiver or a scheduling control plane, and because the paid step is a prepaid 30-day block rather than a subscription it can be switched on for one month of load and left off afterwards.

limits.value: 250 MB of disk and 128 MB of RAM per app is the wall: it fits a small API and not a build plus a runtime plus data.

notes: Aggregator claim checked: free-for.dev lists '1 app with 0.25 vCPU, 128 MB RAM, 250 MB disk, and 100 GB bandwidth'. The vendor matches on every number, so the gap is zero here. What the aggregator omits: the read-only root filesystem with one writable volume at /data, no managed database, a single region, and that Starter and Pro are prepaid 30-day blocks renewed by hand through PayPal rather than subscriptions.
